claims.text: Atmospheric plasma spraying can deposit an AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating on SS316L.
Furnace annealing of the coated SS316L induces interdiffusion between the AlCoCrFeNi coating and the substrate.
Coating and annealing create an interdiffused interfacial region.
Coating and annealing create a stable, passivated surface microstructure in the high-entropy-alloy coating.
The annealing-induced surface microstructure has a lower defect density.
The annealing-induced surface microstructure hampers ion transport.
Annealing-induced interdiffusion produces a gradient microstructure.
The gradient microstructure diminishes galvanic coupling between the coating and substrate.
The passivated interdiffused layer reduces the number of active corrosion sites.
The passivated interdiffused layer limits diffusion pathways for corrosive species.
The interdiffused, passivated layer acts as a protective corrosion barrier.
Annealed AlCoCrFeNi-coated SS316L will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than bare SS316L under identical corrosive conditions.
Annealed AlCoCrFeNi-coated SS316L will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than coated but unannealed SS316L under identical corrosive conditions.
Annealed coated SS316L will exhibit improved electrochemical impedance or polarization behavior relative to both controls.

The proposed protection should persist in chemical-processing and nuclear-power environments while temperature, chemical aggressiveness, and mechanical stress remain within the stability range of the annealed microstructure.
Prior initial evidence supports improved corrosion resistance from the combination of coating and annealing.
